articles.title: Xi on his DC visit: ‘China and the US should be partners not rivals’
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: China’s President Xi Jinping concluded his three-day state visit to the US on Friday, September 25, with hopes of enhanced cooperation and partnership between the world’s two largest economies. Xi arrived in the US on Wednesday and received a large-scale welcome from President Donald Trump. Though this was their third in-person meeting it was Xi’s first state visit to the US in over a decade. On Thursday, the leaders had a long in-person conversation in the White House and finished the day with a state dinner with 130 guests, including tech executives. articles.title: German students say ‘we don’t want to go to war’
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Thousands of students across Germany were once again on strike against conscription and militarization on Friday, September 25. Actions took place in at least 100 localities as young people demanded a sharp turn from the government’s chosen path. “We don’t want to be forced into military service and we don’t want to go to war,” the students wrote in declaration after their last strike in May. Read more: German students expand their strike against conscription and militarization to 150 cities This is the fourth time students have exchanged classrooms for streets since the end of 2025 . articles.title: Trump’s war on the ICC is bigger than Netanyahu, with Noura Erakat
articles.author: Zoe Alexandra
articles.content_excerpt: The Trump administration’s assault on the ICC isn’t just about protecting Netanyahu from war crimes prosecution. It’s about preserving “imperial impunity” – Israel’s just “the smokescreen,” says Noura Erakat, professor of criminal justice and Africana studies at Rutgers University and human rights attorney. She traces Washington’s bipartisan refusal to ratify the Rome Statute to explain why the International Criminal Court has spent two decades indicting mostly African and Arab leaders. The 2024 warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli defense minister Yoav Gallant just show the court “between a rock and a hard place”: finally give up its legitimacy entirely, or face destruction by the US. articles.title: Trump needs China, Xi is playing the long game, with Amanda Yee
articles.author: Rania Khalek
articles.content_excerpt: Chinese President Xi Jinping “holds all the cards” as he meets with Trump on Thursday, says Amanda Yee, host of BreakThrough News’ The China Report. She joins Zoe Alexandra and Rania Khalek to break down Xi’s first White House visit in 11 years. With Trump facing a massively unpopular war on Iran, surging inflation, growing resistance to ICE terror – and with US midterms weeks away – Washington wants quick deals it can sell as big wins. But Yee says Beijing is playing a longer game, with massive implications for the global future.
